faq.a: Indira is associated with the Sanskrit form إِنْدِيرَا, whose core sense is indira; beauty, splendour (sanskrit).

faq.q: What is the origin of Indira?
faq.a: Indira is associated with Sanskrit. Indira is Sanskrit इन्दिरा (indirā), meaning 'beauty, splendour'. It is used as a female given name in South and Central Asia.
No — the underlying form is Sanskrit, not Arabic.
Indira can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Sanskrit-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Indira should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Indirā is a Sanskrit name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Indira mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Indira is rendered اندرا and carries the sense اندرا، خوبصورتی.

faq.q: What does Indira mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Indira is rendered اندرا and carries the sense اندرا، زیبایی.
A romanized syllable approximation is in-di-ra. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Indira?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Indira, indira. Script forms are إِنْدِيرَا, اندرا, इंदिरा.

faq.q: Is Indira a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
